title: At a Restaurant
goal: Reserve or request a table, order with relevant needs, explain a problem, and settle the check.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: How many people are in your party?

turns.en: How many people are in your party?

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Four. We have a reservation for seven under Chen.

turns.en: Four. We have a reservation for seven under Chen.

turns.speaker: Host

runs.text: Yes, I have it here. Your table is ready.

turns.en: Yes, I have it here. Your table is ready.

runs.text: gives the reservation name. Without a reservation, try
Do you have a table for two?
The answer may include a wait:
Can we put our name on the list?
I'd like to make a reservation for four this Friday at seven
. Staff may confirm a date or offer another time. Ask about a practical need instead of assuming it:
Can you accommodate a group of eight?
Use this fictional menu and information in Practice:

rows.text: Pasta with vegetables and tomato sauce; $15
Greens and tomatoes; dressing served separately; $5
Baked apples with vanilla ice cream; $7

runs.text: The restaurant can leave the cream out of the soup. Its kitchen handles peanuts, and staff cannot assure the guest that peanut cross-contact is prevented. Cash and cards are accepted; separate checks are available if requested before ordering. These are facts for this practice scene.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Could I ask about the soup first? Can you make it without cream?

turns.en: Could I ask about the soup first? Can you make it without cream?

turns.speaker: Server

runs.text: Yes, we can leave that out.

turns.en: Yes, we can leave that out.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Then I'll have the soup without cream and the vegetable pasta.

turns.en: Then I'll have the soup without cream and the vegetable pasta.

blocks.caption: Order and ask about ingredients · Server & Guest

runs.text: Could I have the dressing on the side?
can mean the main dish in American usage.
An allergy statement needs more precision than a dislike:

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: I have a peanut allergy. Does the dish contain peanuts, and can you check how it's prepared?

turns.en: I have a peanut allergy. Does the dish contain peanuts, and can you check how it's prepared?

turns.speaker: Server

runs.text: It has no peanuts in the recipe, but we handle peanuts in the kitchen and can't assure you there won't be cross-contact.

turns.en: It has no peanuts in the recipe, but we handle peanuts in the kitchen and can't assure you there won't be cross-contact.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Thanks for checking. I won't order food here today.

turns.en: Thanks for checking. I won't order food here today.

blocks.caption: Order and ask about ingredients · Guest & Server

runs.text: means an allergen gets into food unintentionally, including through shared preparation equipment. Ingredient absence and a statement about preparation are different information. The exchange practices asking and responding; a menu name alone cannot establish suitability for a particular allergy.
rather than wait for a server to guess.

rows.text: Main plate / smaller plate for an accompanying item

runs.text: Could we have a few more minutes?
It's a little too salty for me
expresses a less positive one. You can have different opinions from your companion.
For something that needs attention, identify the mismatch:

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Excuse me. I ordered the vegetable pasta, but this is fish.

turns.en: Excuse me. I ordered the vegetable pasta, but this is fish.

turns.speaker: Server

runs.text: I'm sorry. I'll check the order.

turns.en: I'm sorry. I'll check the order.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: Thank you. Could you bring the pasta instead?

turns.en: Thank you. Could you bring the pasta instead?

blocks.caption: Evaluate or report a problem · Guest & Server

runs.text: We haven't received the salad yet
requests a remedy. A clear problem report is useful; you do not need to call the food wonderful before describing it.

turns.speaker: Guest

runs.text: No, thanks. I'm full. Could we get the check?

turns.en: No, thanks. I'm full. Could we get the check?

runs.text: identify the amount to pay. Ask
Can we split the check evenly?
to divide the total equally. These are different requests, and availability depends on the restaurant.
offers to pay. A companion can accept or say
I'd prefer to pay for my own meal
This lesson does not set a universal charge or tipping amount.
Speak both roles alone, using the menu and scene facts above.
Arrive for the four-person Chen reservation at seven. The host asks about your party and reservation name.
Order soup without cream and vegetable pasta. Ask for a few more minutes before deciding on dessert.

Change the need: your character has a peanut allergy. Ask about ingredients and preparation. Staff give the supplied kitchen information; respond without turning their uncertainty into a safety guarantee.
You ordered pasta but received fish. Describe the mistake and request the correct dish. Staff agree to check it.
You and a companion disagree about the fish. One thinks it is delicious; the other finds it too salty. Then decline dessert and request the check.
Hide the models. Repeat the visit with a two-person walk-in party, grilled fish for your order, and separate checks requested before ordering. If told the wait is twenty minutes, accept or leave.
Four people. We have a reservation under Chen for seven.
Can you make the soup without cream? — Yes. — I'll have that and the vegetable pasta.
Can you check how it's prepared?
Thanks. I won't order food here today.
I ordered vegetable pasta, but this is fish. Could you bring the pasta instead?
It's delicious. — It's too salty for me.
No dessert, thanks. Could we get the check?
Do you have a table for two? Could we have separate checks when we order?
Did you distinguish an ingredient preference from an allergy question? Did your problem report match what happened? Did both people understand how they intended to pay?

ja: 席・注文・困りごと・会計。
note: 食材の好みと、アレルギーについての確認は別です。間違った料理が来たら、頼んだ物と実際に来た物を分けて伝えます。
